title.en: Volume 212 Tables 52: Diplomatic Missions Chronological Table 1, Chinese Envoys Abroad
title.raw: 卷212 表五十二 交聘年表一 中国遣驻使

translations.literal: The institution of exchange missions was at its height in the Spring and Autumn period.
translations.idiomatic: The rituals of diplomatic exchange reached their fullest expression in the Spring and Autumn era.

sentences.zh: 南北史本紀書交聘頗詳。

translations.literal: The basic annals of the Northern and Southern Histories record exchange missions in considerable detail.
translations.idiomatic: The reign annals of the Northern and Southern Histories treat diplomatic exchanges at length.

sentences.zh: 其時中土分裂，與列國之敵體相交，無以異也。

translations.literal: At that time the central lands were divided; dealings with the various states as equal rivals were no different.
translations.idiomatic: In that age the Central Plain was fractured; treating with other powers as peer states differed little from what would follow.

sentences.zh: 宋與遼金歲賀正旦、賀生辰外，有泛使，今謂之專使。

translations.literal: Apart from the Song's annual congratulations on New Year's Day and birthdays with Liao and Jin, there were general envoys, now called special envoys.
translations.idiomatic: Beyond the Song's yearly New Year and birthday missions to Liao and Jin, there were general envoys—what we now call special envoys.

sentences.zh: 然皆事畢即行，不常駐，《金史》有盟聘表。

translations.literal: Yet all departed when their business was done and did not remain permanently; the History of Jin has a table of alliances and missions.
translations.idiomatic: Yet they all left when their business was finished and were not permanently resident; the History of Jin includes a table of alliances and missions.

sentences.zh: 清有中夏，沿元明制，視海內外莫與爲對。

translations.literal: When the Qing possessed the Middle Kingdom, following Yuan and Ming systems, it regarded none within or beyond the seas as its equal.
translations.idiomatic: Once the Qing held the Central Realm, following Yuan and Ming precedent, it acknowledged no peer at home or abroad.

sentences.zh: 凡俄、英之來聘者，國史皆書曰來貢。

translations.literal: For all who came on missions from Russia and Britain, the state histories all recorded them as coming to offer tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Envoys from Russia, Britain, and the like were invariably entered in the dynastic records as coming to present tribute.

sentences.zh: 洎道光庚子訂約，始與敵體相等。

translations.literal: When treaties were concluded in the gengzi year of Daoguang, they began to be treated as equal rival states.
translations.idiomatic: Only after the treaties of the Daoguang gengzi year (1840) were foreign powers recognized as coequal states.

sentences.zh: 咸豐庚申之役，肇衅非一，而遣使駐京未允實行者，亦一大端。

translations.literal: In the gengshen campaign of Xianfeng there were many causes of conflict, and the failure to grant and implement the dispatch of ministers resident in Beijing was also a major issue.
translations.idiomatic: The Xianfeng gengshen war had more than one provocation; the refusal to allow—and implement—resident ministers in Beijing was itself a major grievance.

sentences.zh: 自是而後，有約各國率遣使駐京。

translations.literal: From then on, by treaty each country generally dispatched ministers resident in Beijing.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter treaty powers routinely posted ministers to the capital.

sentences.zh: 同治中，志剛、孫家穀之出，是爲中國遣專使之始。

translations.literal: In the Tongzhi period, the departures of Zhigang and Sun Jiagu were the beginning of China's dispatching special envoys.
translations.idiomatic: During Tongzhi, the missions of Zhigang and Sun Jiagu marked China's first dispatch of special envoys abroad.

sentences.zh: 光緒建元，郭嵩燾、陳蘭彬諸人分使英、美，是爲中國遣駐使之始。

translations.literal: When Guangxu began his reign, Guo Songtao, Chen Lanbin, and others were separately sent to Britain and America—this was the beginning of China's dispatching resident ministers.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Guangxu reign, Guo Songtao, Chen Lanbin, and others were assigned to Britain and the United States—the start of permanently resident Chinese missions.

sentences.zh: 其時以使俄者兼德、奧，使英者兼法、義、比，使美者兼日斯巴尼亞、秘魯，而日本無附近之國，則特置使。

translations.literal: At that time the envoy to Russia also covered Germany and Austria; the envoy to Britain also covered France, Italy, and Belgium; the envoy to America also covered Spain and Peru; and because Japan had no nearby country to share, a separate minister was appointed.
translations.idiomatic: Initially the minister to Russia doubled for Germany and Austria; the minister to Britain for France, Italy, and Belgium; and the minister to the United States for Spain and Peru—while Japan, with no neighboring power to share a mission, received its own minister.

sentences.zh: 甲午以後，增置漸多，迄于宣統，俄、英、法、德、和、比、義、奧、日本皆特置使，日斯巴尼亞則改以法使兼，秘魯、墨西哥、古巴則以美使兼。

translations.literal: After the Jiawu year, appointments increased gradually; by the Xuantong period Russia, Britain, France, Germany, the Netherlands, Belgium, Italy, Austria, and Japan all had separate ministers; Spain was thereafter covered by the French minister, and Peru, Mexico, and Cuba by the American minister.
translations.idiomatic: After 1894 postings multiplied; by the Xuantong era Russia, Britain, France, Germany, the Netherlands, Belgium, Italy, Austria, and Japan each had dedicated ministers, while Spain fell under the French legation and Peru, Mexico, and Cuba under the American.

translations.literal: A minister to Korea was appointed and soon abolished.
translations.idiomatic: A mission to Korea was established only to be withdrawn shortly afterward.

sentences.zh: 有約之國，惟葡萄牙、瑞典、那威、丹馬諸國無駐使，有事則以就近駐使任之。

translations.literal: Among treaty countries, only Portugal, Sweden, Norway, and Denmark had no resident ministers; when business arose the nearest resident minister handled it.
translations.idiomatic: Of the treaty powers, only Portugal, Sweden, Norway, and Denmark lacked resident ministers; matters were referred to whichever legation lay nearest.

sentences.zh: 國際交涉，大至和戰之重，細至節文之末，爲使者罔弗與聞，關國家休戚者固至重也。

translations.literal: In international dealings, from weighty matters of war and peace down to the minutiae of ceremonial protocol, there is nothing envoys do not hear of; what bears on the nation's weal and woe is indeed of the utmost importance.
translations.idiomatic: International affairs range from war and peace to the finest points of protocol, and envoys are party to all of it—work that touches the nation's fortunes is plainly vital.
